newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH C.BANK PLEASED WITH PRESENT ZLOTY RATE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH C.BANK PLEASED WITH PRESENT ZLOTY RATE.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland, the central bank, is pleased with the current zloty exchange rate, the bank's deputy president Witold Kozinski said on Thursday.
"We are pleased with the current level the zloty," Kozinski told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

On Thursday the zloty traded just below three percent from the central parity rate -- the centre of the local currency's 14-percent daily trading band -- and was fixed the central bank around 2.90 percent from parity.
Kozinski said the central bank, which repeatedly intervened against the zloty in January, could further intervene on the forex market in future. He declined to elaborate.
He said also that January's central bank currency-buying interventions showed that the Polish forex market was shallow.
"They showed that the market was shallow," Kozinski said.
Last month the zloty strengthened to four percent from the parity rate on speculative currency-sales and foreign investor entry into Polish treasuries, especially five-year bonds.
